title: Electromagnetic induction — generators
examTip: Electromagnetic induction is the reverse of the motor effect. There are two ways to induce an EMF. Move a conductor through a magnetic field, OR change the magnetic field through a coil. No movement (or no change) = no induced EMF.
introTips: Electromagnetic induction is how almost all the electricity in the national grid is generated.
To induce an EMF, the conductor and the magnetic field must move relative to each other.
Faster movement, stronger magnets and more coil turns all increase the induced EMF.
An AC generator gives a sinusoidal (wave-shaped) output. The voltage reverses every half turn.
Fleming's right-hand rule is for generators. The left-hand rule is for motors. They are different.
intro: When you switch on a light, its electricity was almost certainly made by electromagnetic induction. That happens in a power station, where a turbine spins inside magnetic coils. In 1831, Michael Faraday discovered that moving a magnet through a coil of wire makes an electric current. That discovery changed everything. Induction is at work in power station generators. It is in the microphone you speak into on a phone call. It powers a bicycle dynamo and regenerative braking on an electric car. It is the engine behind modern electrical life. Understanding it means understanding how the world gets its power.

keyPoints.heading: What is electromagnetic induction?
keyPoints.content: Electromagnetic induction is when an electromotive force (EMF) is produced by a changing magnetic field through a conductor (or coil). If the circuit is complete, a current flows too. This happens in two ways: (1) Moving a conductor through a magnetic field. For example, moving a wire between two magnets. The wire 'cuts' through magnetic field lines. (2) Changing the magnetic field through a stationary coil. For example, moving a magnet in and out of a coil. Or changing the current in a nearby coil, as in a transformer. Key point: with no relative motion and no change in magnetic field, there is no induced EMF. A stationary conductor in a constant magnetic field feels nothing. The induced EMF drives a current in the conductor. This is how generators make electricity.
writeBullets: An EMF is induced when a conductor moves through a magnetic field (cutting field lines)
An EMF is also induced when the magnetic field through a coil changes
No movement AND no field change = no induced EMF
If the circuit is complete, the induced EMF drives an induced current
This is the reverse of the motor effect. A generator turns kinetic energy into electrical energy

keyTerms.def: The production of an EMF (and current if circuit is complete) when a conductor moves through a magnetic field or experiences a changing magnetic field
An electromotive force produced by electromagnetic induction; drives a current around a circuit if the circuit is complete

keyPoints.memTip: Motor: electricity in → movement out. Generator: movement in → electricity out.
keyPoints.tutor_note: People often say 'the magnet creates electricity'. In fact, induction comes from relative movement between the conductor and the field. A stationary magnet next to a stationary wire produces nothing.

keyPoints.heading: Factors that increase the induced EMF
keyPoints.content: The size of the induced EMF depends on three things. So does the current, if the resistance stays the same. (1) Speed of movement: move the conductor or magnet faster → a larger EMF. (2) Strength of the magnetic field: a stronger magnet → a larger EMF. (3) Number of turns in the coil: more turns → a larger EMF. This is because more conductor cuts through field lines. The direction of the induced EMF (and current) can be reversed. Reverse the direction of movement, or reverse the magnetic field by flipping the magnet. Lenz's law describes the direction. The induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the change that caused it. It works like magnetic braking. The induced current makes its own magnetic field, which resists the magnet's motion. This follows from conservation of energy.
writeBullets: Faster movement → larger induced EMF
Stronger magnetic field → larger induced EMF
More turns on the coil → larger induced EMF
Reverse the direction of movement OR flip the magnet → the induced current reverses
Lenz's law — the induced current opposes the change that caused it (energy conservation)

keyTerms.def: The induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the change producing it; a consequence of conservation of energy

keyPoints.memTip: To increase the induced EMF: go Faster, use a Stronger field, use More turns. F-S-M.
keyPoints.tutor_note: Lenz's law often comes up as 'explain why it's hard to push the magnet into the coil'. The induced current creates a magnetic field. That field repels the approaching magnet.

keyPoints.heading: The AC generator
keyPoints.content: An AC generator (alternator) turns kinetic energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction. A coil of wire is rotated inside a magnetic field. Or a magnet is rotated inside a fixed coil, which works the same way. As the coil rotates, it keeps cutting through magnetic field lines. This induces an EMF. The EMF reaches the outside circuit through slip rings and brushes. A DC motor uses a split-ring commutator instead. Slip rings let the coil rotate freely in one direction, while keeping electrical contact. The rate at which the coil cuts field lines rises and falls smoothly. It is greatest when the coil is parallel to the field, and zero when it is perpendicular. So the output is a sinusoidal alternating current (AC). The voltage reverses direction every half turn. To increase the output voltage: spin faster, use a stronger magnet or add more turns.
writeBullets: AC generator — a coil rotates in a magnetic field. Continuous induction → an alternating EMF
Slip rings and brushes — allow non-stop rotation while keeping electrical contact
The output is sinusoidal AC. The voltage reverses every half turn
Maximum EMF when the coil is parallel to the field (cutting field lines fastest)
Zero EMF when the coil is perpendicular to the field (for a moment, not cutting field lines)

keyTerms.def: A device that converts kinetic energy to electrical energy by rotating a coil in a magnetic field, producing alternating current
Continuous rings in an AC generator that allow the coil to rotate freely while maintaining electrical contact, producing AC output
Current that repeatedly reverses direction; the output of a generator; represented as a sinusoidal wave

keyPoints.memTip: Generator = slip rings (free to spin) → AC output. Motor = split-ring commutator (reverses current) → DC input.
keyPoints.tutor_note: Slip rings (generators, AC) and split-ring commutators (motors, DC) are easy to mix up. Be able to explain what each one does, not just name it.

keyPoints.heading: The microphone and Fleming's right-hand rule
keyPoints.content: A microphone works by electromagnetic induction. It is the reverse of a loudspeaker. Sound waves make a diaphragm vibrate. This moves a coil of wire within a magnetic field. As the coil moves back and forth, it induces an alternating EMF. The EMF copies the pattern of the sound wave. So it makes an electrical signal that represents the original sound. Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of the induced current in a conductor moving through a magnetic field. Use your right hand: - the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic Field - the thumb points in the direction of Motion - the middle finger points in the direction of the induced Current Note: right hand = generator and induction. Left hand = motor effect. This difference is often tested directly.
writeBullets: Microphone — sound waves move a coil in a magnetic field → an induced AC electrical signal
The induced signal copies the pattern of the sound wave
Fleming's right-hand rule — for induction and generators (right hand = generator)
Right hand: index = Field, thumb = Motion, middle = induced Current
Left hand = motor effect. Right hand = generator and induction. Don't mix them up

keyTerms.def: A device using electromagnetic induction to convert sound waves into electrical signals; the reverse of a loudspeaker
Used to find the direction of induced current when a conductor moves through a magnetic field: index=field, thumb=motion, middle=current

keyPoints.memTip: Right hand = generator (makes electricity). Left hand = motor (uses electricity).
keyPoints.tutor_note: Compare the microphone and the loudspeaker directly. Both have a coil and a magnet. But one turns sound into electricity, and the other turns electricity into sound.

0.question: A bar magnet is held still next to a coil of wire. The coil is connected to a galvanometer (current meter). What does the galvanometer read?
options: Zero. No EMF is induced, because there is no relative movement
A steady DC current, proportional to the field strength
An alternating current, because the magnet is magnetic
A current only if the coil has many turns
0.correctFeedback: Correct! Electromagnetic induction needs relative movement or a changing field. A stationary magnet by a stationary coil produces no change. So no EMF is induced.
0.wrongFeedback: A stationary magnet next to a stationary coil induces no EMF. There is no relative motion, and no change in the magnetic field through the coil. You need movement or a changing field to induce an EMF.

1.question: Which of these changes would increase the EMF induced in a generator?
options: Reducing the number of turns on the coil
1.correctFeedback: Correct! Faster spinning → field lines are cut more quickly → a larger induced EMF. The other options would all reduce the EMF or have no effect.
1.wrongFeedback: To increase the induced EMF: spin faster, use a stronger magnet or add more coil turns. Fewer turns or a weaker magnet would decrease the EMF.

3.question: An AC generator has slip rings. A DC motor has a split-ring commutator. What is the key difference?
options: Slip rings allow free non-stop rotation, giving AC. The commutator reverses the current every half turn to keep DC rotation going
Slip rings increase voltage. The commutator increases current
Slip rings are used in motors. The commutator is used in generators
There is no difference. They are two names for the same part
3.correctFeedback: Exactly right! Slip rings let the coil rotate freely and give an AC output. The commutator reverses the current every half turn. This keeps a DC motor spinning in one direction.
3.wrongFeedback: Slip rings (generator) allow free non-stop rotation → AC output. The split-ring commutator (DC motor) reverses the current every half turn to keep it rotating. They differ completely in design and purpose.

commonMistakes: Saying a stationary magnet near a coil induces a current. Induction needs relative movement or a changing magnetic field. No movement = no EMF.
Using the left-hand rule instead of the right-hand rule for induction and generators. Left hand = motor effect. Right hand = generator and induction.
Mixing up slip rings (AC generators) and split-ring commutators (DC motors). They are different parts with different jobs.
Saying more coil turns increases the current directly. More turns increases the induced EMF. The current that results also depends on the circuit's resistance.
Describing Lenz's law wrongly. The induced current opposes the change (the magnet's motion), not the magnetic field itself.
examTips: You may be asked how to increase a generator's induced EMF. Give three separate answers: faster rotation, a stronger magnet and more turns of wire.
Tell generators and motors apart in your answers. Generator = kinetic → electrical. Motor = electrical → kinetic. Both use a magnetic field.
For Lenz's law questions, say that the induced current creates a magnetic field that opposes the magnet's motion. That is why it takes force to push the magnet in.
Sketch the AC generator output as a sine wave. Show the voltage switching between positive and negative every half turn of the coil.
Microphone questions often appear with loudspeaker questions. Be clear which way the energy is converted in each device.
revisionCardBullets: Electromagnetic induction — an EMF is induced when a conductor moves through a field, OR the field through a coil changes
No movement and no change → no induced EMF
Larger EMF: faster movement, a stronger field, more coil turns
Lenz's law — the induced current opposes the change that produces it (energy conservation)
AC generator — a coil rotating in a field, with slip rings. Sinusoidal AC output
Slip rings — allow free rotation and give an AC output
Split-ring commutator (motor) — reverses the current to give non-stop rotation
Maximum EMF when the coil is parallel to the field. Zero EMF when it is perpendicular
Fleming's right-hand rule — for induction and generators: index=field, thumb=motion, middle=current
Microphone — an induction device. Sound → the coil moves in the field → an electrical signal
Motor (left hand) = electricity in. Generator (right hand) = electricity out
